agent.name: VXCore agent
agent.initial1: Hi, I'm the VXCore agent. I noticed oxmysql lost its connection twice in the last hour. Do you want me to review the database config?
agent.initial2: Yes, what can I do to keep it from going down?
agent.replyConfig: The usual culprit is max_connections. I'd suggest raising it to 200 and adding a healthcheck every 30s. I've prepared the change in the editor — you can review it before saving.
agent.replyCrash: I analyzed the logs: the crash comes from a resource that accesses the DB without retries. I can wrap that call with automatic retry (with a backup included).
agent.replyRestart: I can schedule a nightly restart at 04:00 with a notice on your community's Discord. Shall I activate it?
agent.replyDefault: I checked the server status: everything looks good. Do you want me to look at a resource, the logs or set up an automation?
agent.applied: Done: the change is saved with a backup. You can revert it from the editor at any time.

items.q: Does it work with my FXServer?
items.a: Yes. VXCore connects to any modern FXServer (txAdmin, standalone or your own setup) through its RCON console and WebSocket. In under 5 minutes your server shows up in the panel.
No. If you know how to use a browser, you know how to use VXCore. The console, logs and editor are designed so anyone on the team can manage without fear of breaking anything.

items.q: Can the AI agent break my server?
items.a: No. The agent only stages changes in the editor: nothing is written to production until you hit Save, and there's always a copy of the previous version to revert to.

items.q: What about my resources from the Urantix store?
items.a: The VXCore marketplace is integrated with the Urantix store: buy, download and install resources directly on your server from the panel, no FTP or manual deploys.

items.q: Can I change or cancel my plan anytime?
items.a: Of course. Upgrade, downgrade or cancel in one click from your billing panel. Annual plans are prorated if you change before the year is up.
The Pro plan includes priority support with an average first response of under 2 hours. Every plan gets access to the docs, the community and the official Urantix Discord.

cookies.title: Cookie policy
cookies.description: VXCore only uses cookies that are strictly necessary to sign in. No analytics, no ads.
cookies.intro: Short version: VXCore only uses the cookies needed for you to sign in. No analytics, no ads, no third-party tracking.

blocks.text: A small file a site stores in your browser to remember something between one page and the next. Some are essential for the site to work; others measure audiences or show ads. **Here we only use the first kind.**
All of them are **strictly necessary** and are set by Auth.js, the library that manages sign-in. They're marked as `HttpOnly` and `Secure`, so no script can read them and they only travel over HTTPS.

rows.name: __Host-authjs.csrf-token
rows.purpose: Protects the sign-in form against forged requests from other sites (CSRF).

rows.name: __Secure-authjs.callback-url
rows.purpose: Remembers which page to return to when you finish signing in with Google or Discord.

rows.name: __Secure-authjs.session-token
rows.purpose: Keeps you signed in so the panel knows who you are. Only created when you sign in.

sections.heading: Why we don't ask for consent

blocks.text: Cookie law requires consent for cookies that *aren't* essential: analytics, ads, embedded social networks. Since we don't use any of those, there's nothing to consent to, which is why you won't see a banner. If we ever add analytics, the corresponding notice will appear and you'll be able to decline it.

sections.heading: Other data stored in your browser

blocks.text: Your theme preference (light or dark) is stored in your browser's **local storage**, not in a cookie. It never leaves your device and never reaches us.
You can delete or block cookies from your browser settings. Keep in mind they're essential for your session, so blocking them will prevent you from signing in and accessing your panel.

When you make a payment, the process happens on **Stripe's** domain, which applies its own cookie policy. The same happens when you sign in on **Google** or **Discord** screens. We don't set cookies in your browser on behalf of those services.

index.title: Documentation center
index.description: Everything you need to install VXCore, connect your server and set up the Discord bot, explained step by step.

blocks.text: VXCore is the operating system for your FXServer: a **panel** that manages your servers, resources, logs and automations, an **agent** that runs on the same machine as your server, and a **desktop** app for Windows.
Start here
In under 10 minutes you'll have VXCore up and running. Pick the path that fits what you're looking for:

items.title: Installation guide
items.description: Download the installer, activate it with your license and connect your FXServer.

items.title: System requirements
items.description: What you need before starting: operating system, Node and your server.

items.title: Set up the Discord bot
items.description: Connect your community: staff sign-in, roles and server status.

blocks.text: What about deployment?

**You don't have to do anything.** The desktop app starts the panel and the agent on your machine, installs whatever is missing (the Visual C++ runtime and your FXServer if you don't have one) and updates itself. No servers, no Vercel, no code.
Architecture at a glance

head: Piece
Technology
Where it runs
rows: On the same machine as FXServer

blocks.text: The panel **never touches disk or processes**: all of its calls go over HTTP to a VXCore agent, which is what controls FXServer, MySQL, Discord and automations. The agent listens only on `127.0.0.1` (loopback) on purpose: Windows Firewall doesn't ask for network permissions and no ports are exposed.

requirements.title: System requirements
requirements.description: What you need before installing VXCore. Less than you think.

blocks.text: The bare minimum

items: **Windows 10 or 11**, 64-bit.
**~500 MB** of free disk space.
Internet connection (initial download, license activation and updates).
An account on the VXCore website, to get your **license** and the installer.

blocks.text: What the app installs for you
On first launch the app checks your machine and **downloads and installs whatever is missing**, with nothing to do on your side:

items: **Visual C++ 2015-2022 (x64) runtime**: FXServer needs it to start. The first time, the app will ask for administrator permission (UAC).
**FXServer artifacts**: if you don't have a server yet, the app downloads the build recommended by FiveM and leaves it ready in your user folder.

blocks.text: What you DON'T need

items: **Node.js or npm**: the app ships with its own integrated runtime.
**MySQL** to get started: you only need it if your server uses a database.
**Git**, or any coding skills.

blocks.text: Already have an FXServer? You can **register** it from the panel and VXCore controls it just the same. On Linux or a VPS? The agent also runs on Linux, but the desktop app is Windows-only.

installation.title: Installation guide
installation.description: Download, activate and connect VXCore step by step.

blocks.text: 1. Create your account
Go to the website and **sign in with Google or Discord**. Once your account exists you reach your panel, where your license and the installer live.
2. Download the installer
From your **panel** (the *Download* button in the Installer card) you get the `VXCore-Setup` executable. You don't need Node or any other program installed.
3. Run it and enter your license
Run the installer and, when asked, paste the **license key** shown in your panel. The key is tied to your account: don't share it.
4. First launch: the app sets everything up

When you open the app for the first time it checks your machine and **installs whatever is missing automatically** (the Visual C++ runtime and, if you don't have one, your FXServer). You'll just have to accept a Windows prompt (UAC) the first time.
5. Connect your server
Create a new server from the panel or **register** an existing one by pointing to its folder. In under 5 minutes your server appears in the console, logs and every other module.
Deployment and updates

**You don't deploy anything.** The app starts the panel and the agent on your machine, shuts them down when you close the window and updates arrive by **auto-update**: the panel notifies you when there's a new version and it installs itself without you having to download anything again.
Want your community to sign in with Discord? Follow the **Set up the Discord bot** guide.

discord.title: Set up the Discord bot
discord.description: Connect VXCore to your Discord server: staff sign-in, roles, status and whitelist.

blocks.text: With the bot connected, your community signs in to the panel with **their Discord account**, staff is recognized by **roles**, and you can publish the **server status** in a channel. Everything is configured from *Settings → Discord & Staff*.
1. Create an application in the Discord Developer Portal
Go to **https://discord.com/developers/applications**, click *New Application*, give it a name (for example, your server's) and create it.
2. Copy the credentials

items: **Client ID**: under the *OAuth2* tab.
**Client Secret**: under *OAuth2 → General*.
**Bot Token**: under *Bot → Reset Token*. It's a secret: don't share it.
**Guild ID**: in Discord, enable *Developer Mode* (Settings → Advanced), right-click your server → *Copy Server ID*.

blocks.text: 3. Invite the bot to your server
In *OAuth2 → URL Generator*, tick the **bot** scope with the permissions you want, copy the generated URL and open it in your browser to add the bot.
4. Configure it in the app
Open *Settings → Discord & Staff* in the panel and paste the credentials. Save, and the bot will connect to your server.
What you can do next

items: **Sign in with Discord**: your community logs in with their account; you decide who is *owner*, *admin* or *moderator* by assigning roles.
**Server status**: publish in a channel whether your FiveM server is online, how many players are on and more.
**Whitelist**: restrict access to your server to members of your Discord.

blocks.text: The **Client Secret** and the **Bot Token** are secrets: never share them or push them to GitHub.
